documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Darren is a 56 yo carpenter (self-employed, does mostly finish work and decks) transferring care. His prior PCP retired and the office closed; records release signed today.

Diabetes: told he had type 2 DM this past spring on routine bloodwork. Started metformin, worked up to 1000 mg BID over a few weeks. GI upset at first, now fine. Checks sugars rarely. No hypoglycemia, no polyuria. Has not had an eye exam since diagnosis.

Other history: none he knows of. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: dad had a heart attack at 64 and high BP. Mom has type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol. An uncle on mom's side had a stroke at 70.
Social: smokes about half a pack a day, started around 20. Has tried to quit on his own a couple of times. Beer with friends maybe once or twice a week. Works for himself, lots of lifting and kneeling. Right handed. Plays guitar.

ROS: negative except as above. No chest pain with work, no dyspnea, no claudication, no vision change, no foot numbness.

Exam: well appearing. BP 134/84 single reading, will recheck at next visit. BMI 32. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal bilaterally, DP/PT 2+. No edema.

A/P
1. T2DM, on metformin. A1c drawn today. Needs eye exam - list of local optometrists given. Foot exam normal today.
2. Tobacco: half ppd, ~18 pack-yr. Talked about quitting. Not ready to pick a date, open to revisiting.
3. BP 134/84 - above goal for diabetic but one reading. Recheck next visit.
4. Lipids: wants to come back fasting. Order placed.
5. HCM: flu shot today. HCV and HIV screening done today. FIT kit given. Prior records requested.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Darren,

Your A1c came back at 6.9%, which is close to where we want it on metformin, so no changes for now. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were both negative.

When you get a chance, please come by the lab one morning before eating for the cholesterol test. No appointment needed.

And drop the FIT kit in the mail when you can.

Take care

documents.body:
S: Here about the health fair readings (two separate days, 160s/high 90s per pt). Feels well, no complaints. No headaches, chest pain, dyspnea, vision change or leg swelling. First visit back since October - missed the January follow-up. Still on metformin 1000 BID, taking it. Still smoking about half a pack a day.

No carotid bruits. Heart regular, S1 S2 normal, no S3 or murmur. Lungs clear. No edema, distal pulses full. Fundi without obvious hemorrhages on undilated look.

4. Obesity, BMI 32 - as above.
5. Smoking - strongly advised to quit, this is now the single biggest thing he can do. He says he'll think about it. Discussed patch / meds, declines for now.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/04/2022
Referred by: primary care, for type 2 diabetes above target.

History: 57-year-old man (per our intake; DOB 7/26/1964) with type 2 diabetes for a little under two years, managed from the start with metformin, now 1000 mg twice daily, which he tolerates without GI trouble. For the last six months he has been strict with diet (no sugared drinks, smaller portions) and walks most evenings, and still his A1c has climbed. Denies any low sugars, shakiness or sweats. Denies polyuria or blurred vision.
Other history: hypertension on lisinopril, hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father - MI at 64 and hypertension; mother - type 2 diabetes and dyslipidemia; maternal uncle - stroke at 70.
Social: carpenter. Non-smoker currently.

Exam: BP 134/78. BMI 31.
Eyes: dilated-free fundoscopic view shows no diabetic retinopathy.
Neuro: cranial nerves, strength, reflexes and sensation including monofilament and vibration at the toes normal.
Thyroid not enlarged. Feet without ulceration.

Data: A1c 8.2%. Fasting plasma glucose 165 mg/dL. Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL.

Assessment: Type 2 diabetes, inadequately controlled on maximal metformin and lifestyle.

Plan:
- Add glipizide 5 mg each morning before breakfast. Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
- Counselled on hypoglycemia: symptoms, carrying glucose tabs, not skipping breakfast on job days.
- Meter: check fasting and occasional pre-supper.
- A1c at primary care in 3 months; return here as needed.
- Annual dilated eye exam recommended.

Thank you for the referral.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Office Visit - Hand Weakness
documents.author: PCP

CC: R hand weak.

For several months (thinks since early summer) dropping screws and small nails at work, worse lately. Hand feels clumsy, not painful. Little finger tingles off and on. Wore a drugstore wrist brace at night for a few weeks, didn't help. No neck pain. No injury. L hand fine.

Exam: R hand - visible hollowing between thumb and index on the back of the hand and flattening at the base of the little finger compared with left. Weak finger spread on R. Decreased light touch little finger. Wrist and elbow strength ok. Neck ROM full, painless.

A/P: R hand intrinsic weakness with wasting and little-finger numbness - pattern looks like ulnar nerve rather than carpal tunnel (which is what he assumed). Diabetes may contribute. Referral to hand/orthopedics, they will likely want nerve testing. Until then avoid leaning on the elbow.

conditions.label: Ulnar neuropathy at the right elbow (cubital tunnel syndrome)

documents.title: Orthopedic Hand Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
HAND AND UPPER EXTREMITY CLINIC - CONSULTATION
Visit: 01/03/2023
Reason: right hand weakness, referred by primary care.

HPI: 58-year-old right-hand-dominant carpenter. Over several months his right hand has gotten progressively weaker. He has trouble pinching nails between his fingers and steadying stock, and drops screws and washers, particularly when using the ring and little fingers. He has watched the muscle between his fingers and at the base of the little finger slowly thin out. He put it down to age and hard use until it began to slow him at work. No pain, no injury, no fevers or weight loss. He gets intermittent numbness and tingling on the inner side of the hand that comes on when the elbow stays bent for a while or when he rests it on a hard surface. He sleeps with both arms folded under the pillow and some mornings wakes with a numb hand for a few minutes. He leans on his elbows at the bench a lot. A night wrist brace did nothing. Palm grip when shaking hands feels the same, but spreading or pinching between fingers is harder, and guitar chords that need finger spread have become difficult. Left hand normal. No neck history.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Meds: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, social alcohol.

Exam, right upper limb:
- Marked atrophy of the hypothenar eminence and first dorsal interosseous.
- Mild clawing of ring and little fingers at rest.
- Weak finger abduction and adduction; cannot hold a sheet of paper between the fingers against resistance.
- Diminished sensation over the palmar and dorsal little finger and ulnar half of the ring finger.
- Grip mildly reduced. Wrist flexion, elbow flexion/extension, pronation and supination full strength.
- Tapping over the ulnar nerve at the medial elbow produces tingling into the little finger.
- Left: normal. Neck: full painless motion.

Impression: Right cubital tunnel syndrome - ulnar neuropathy at the elbow - with motor and sensory involvement and intrinsic atrophy.

Plan:
- Nerve conduction study / EMG of the right upper limb.
- Elbow pad during the day, night splint holding the elbow straighter; avoid prolonged elbow flexion and leaning on the elbow.
- Follow-up after the study to discuss decompression; given the atrophy, surgery is likely to be recommended.

Hand and Upper Extremity Clinic

reports.text:
Indication: right hand intrinsic weakness and ulnar-distribution numbness.
Nerve conduction: Right ulnar motor, recording abductor digiti minimi and first dorsal interosseous: reduced amplitudes at all sites; conduction velocity 55 m/s in the forearm and 36 m/s across the elbow segment, with a drop in amplitude across the elbow. Right ulnar sensory to the little finger: reduced amplitude. Right dorsal ulnar cutaneous sensory: reduced. Right median motor and sensory: normal. Right radial sensory: normal. Left ulnar motor and sensory: normal.
Needle EMG: Right first dorsal interosseous and abductor digiti minimi: fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves, with large, long-duration motor units and reduced recruitment. Right flexor carpi ulnaris: normal. Right abductor pollicis brevis, extensor indicis, biceps, triceps, deltoid: normal. Cervical paraspinals: normal.
reports.conclusion: Right ulnar neuropathy localized to the elbow, moderate to severe, with both demyelinating and axonal features and active denervation of ulnar-innervated hand muscles. No electrodiagnostic evidence of cervical radiculopathy, brachial plexopathy, or median neuropathy.

procedures.procedure: Nerve conduction study with needle EMG

documents.title: Orthopedic Hand Follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
HAND CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP
Visit: 02/14/2023

Reviewed electrodiagnostic study: right ulnar neuropathy at the elbow, moderate to severe, with denervation in the hand intrinsics.
Since last visit he has used the elbow pad and night splint. Numbness episodes a little less frequent. Weakness unchanged. Exam unchanged from 1/3.

Discussion: given muscle wasting and denervation, I recommended ulnar nerve decompression at the elbow. Reviewed what the operation involves, recovery time off heavy work, and that strength recovery after atrophy is uncertain; the goal is to stop further loss. He is self-employed and has jobs booked through the fall and would like to put surgery off. Reasonable as long as he understands the nerve may not recover as well with time. He will continue the splint and pad and call us when he is ready to schedule.
Allergies: NKDA.

Hand and Upper Extremity Clinic

orders.reason: Exertional chest pressure, diabetes, former smoker - evaluate for angina

documents.title: Office Visit - Chest Pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit (texted last night).

About a month of a pressure feeling in the left chest when he walks in the morning, sometimes going down the left arm. Comes on partway up the hill on his usual loop, goes away within a few minutes of stopping. Never at rest, never at night. Not with meals. Hasn't happened at work, though he says he's been slowing down on ladders. No dyspnea, no palpitations, no lightheadedness.
Risks: diabetes, HTN, HLD, 18 pk-yr ex-smoker, father MI at 64.

Exam: comfortable. BP at goal. Heart regular, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. No edema. Chest wall not tender.
ECG: sinus, normal, no ischemic changes.

A/P: Exertional chest pressure with arm radiation in a diabetic with multiple risk factors - this is angina until proven otherwise, stable pattern. Resting ECG normal.
- Start aspirin 81 mg daily.
- Cardiology referral, asked for an early appointment; RN will call to expedite.
- Hold the morning hill walks until seen; flat walking ok if no symptoms.
- Any chest pain at rest, lasting more than 10-15 min, or with sweating/dyspnea: call 911, chew aspirin.
Continue other meds.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: January 4, 2024
Referring: primary care - exertional chest discomfort.

HISTORY
Mr. Dowd is a 59-year-old self-employed carpenter with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Over roughly two months he has noticed a pressure in the left side of the chest that travels into the left arm during his morning walks. It eases with a few minutes of rest. He has had no episodes at rest. His PCP found a normal resting ECG and started aspirin in December. No dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or syncope.
Risk factors: diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, ex-smoker (quit 2021, about 18 pack-years), obesity, father with MI at 64.

MEDICATIONS: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: none known.

EXAM
BP 138/86, HR 78 regular, BMI 30.
JVP not raised. Carotids without bruit. Heart: regular, normal S1/S2, no murmur, gallop or rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Extremities warm, no edema, pedal pulses present.

ASSESSMENT
Typical exertional angina, stable pattern, in a diabetic man with several risk factors.

PLAN
1. Begin metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
2. Sublingual nitroglycerin 0.4 mg as needed; instructed on use and when to call 911.
3. Continue aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg.
4. Exercise treadmill test.
5. Depending on result, coronary angiography.

ADDENDUM (01/23/2024): Exercise test on 1/9 showed anterior ST depression at high workload. Angiography today: 70% stenosis of the LAD, no other significant disease, normal LV function. We reviewed revascularization versus medical therapy; with stable symptoms and single-vessel disease he prefers medical management. He was offered and agreed to join a randomized, double-blind six-month study comparing an investigational anti-anginal drug with placebo; study medication is dispensed by the research pharmacy and is in addition to his usual regimen. Follow-up in our clinic in 6 months.

Cardiology

reports.text: Protocol: Bruce. Resting ECG sinus rhythm, no ST changes. Resting BP 136/84. Exercised to stage 4; stopped for fatigue and chest pressure. Peak heart rate 92% of age-predicted maximum. BP response appropriate. At high workload, horizontal ST depression developed in V2-V4, resolving by 4 minutes of recovery. Chest pressure at peak, resolved in recovery. No arrhythmia.
reports.conclusion: Positive for exercise-induced anterior ischemia, appearing only at high workload. Good functional capacity.

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 06/24/2025 13:05. Regional hospital ED.

CC: tired and weak x 2 weeks, palpitations

HPI: 60M with type 2 diabetes (metformin, basal insulin), coronary artery disease on medical therapy, HTN, HLD. Two weeks of progressive fatigue and generalized muscle weakness, worse the last few days; struggled to carry sheet goods at work. Intermittent palpitations. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no fainting. Hot weeks working outdoors; thinks he hasn't been drinking enough. No vomiting or diarrhea. No new medicines, no supplements, no salt substitute. No NSAIDs.

Meds (per pt): metformin 1000 BID, insulin glargine 24 u qHS, lisinopril 20, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI at 64, HTN; mother T2DM, dyslipidemia; maternal uncle stroke at 70.
SH: carpenter, self-employed. Former smoker, 18 pk-yr. Alcohol 1-2/wk.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 98, RR 18, T 36.8, SpO2 98% RA. Tired-appearing, alert, oriented. Mucous membranes dry; skin turgor decreased. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Strength 5-/5 symmetric proximally, reflexes 2+ symmetric, no focal deficit. No edema.

Results:
Na 138, K 6.2 (non-hemolyzed), Cl 105, HCO3 18, BUN 29, Cr 1.9 (baseline about 1.0 per records), glucose 198.
Urine pH 6.0.
ECG: sinus 98, T waves not peaked, intervals normal.
Plasma renin activity and aldosterone sent - pending at discharge.

ED course: 1 L normal saline IV. Regular insulin 10 units IV with dextrose 25 g IV, glucose monitored, no hypoglycemia. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g PO x1. Cardiac monitor - sinus, no ectopy. Repeat at 17:45: K 5.4, Cr 1.6. Tolerating fluids by mouth. Symptoms improved.

MDM: Hyperkalemia with a normal-gap-range metabolic acidosis and urine pH 6.0 in a diabetic on an ACE inhibitor, with volume depletion pushing creatinine up. Picture fits type 4 (hyperkalemic) renal tubular acidosis; renin/aldosterone sent to confirm.

Impression: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis (hyperkalemic), hyperkalemia; volume depletion.

Disposition: discharged 20:40.
- HOLD lisinopril and metformin until seen by PCP with repeat labs.
- Continue insulin; may need less while eating less - check sugars.
- Avoid potassium-rich salt substitutes, NSAIDs.
- Push fluids.
- PCP in 2 days for BMP. Return for weakness, palpitations, chest pain, fainting.

Emergency Medicine

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of service: 07/06/2026, arrival 09:15.

Chief complaint: double vision since this morning.

HPI: 61-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension, CAD on medical therapy and type 4 RTA (prior ED visit here June 2025 for hyperkalemia). Woke up fine; double vision came on suddenly while having coffee around 7 am, images side by side and slightly stacked, goes away when he covers either eye. Driven in by a neighbor. No headache. No weakness, numbness, speech trouble, jaw pain with chewing, scalp tenderness or visual loss. No trauma.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, insulin glargine 24 u qHS, lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI at 64 and HTN; mother T2DM and dyslipidemia; maternal uncle stroke at 70.
SH: self-employed carpenter; quit smoking 2021, 18 pack-years; 1-2 drinks/week.

Exam: BP 138/84, HR 72, afebrile, SpO2 98%.
Eyes: at rest the right eye sits down and out. Cannot adduct the right eye or elevate it. Right pupil dilated and sluggish to light; left pupil normal. Visual acuity normal in each eye. Fields full to confrontation.
Facial sensation intact all three divisions. Corneal/lacrimal reflex present on both sides. Remaining cranial nerves normal. Strength, sensation, coordination and gait normal. Temporal arteries nontender.

Results: BMP, CBC unremarkable for him. ESR and CRP normal.
CTA head/neck: no aneurysm, no stenosis or dissection; no hemorrhage.
MRI brain w/wo: normal; no compressive lesion or enhancement of the third nerve, cavernous sinuses normal.

Neurology consult (ED, 14:30): agrees exam is an isolated right third nerve palsy with pupil involvement. With aneurysm and compressive lesions excluded by CTA and MRI and inflammatory markers normal, presumed microvascular (ischemic) palsy related to diabetes and hypertension. Expect gradual improvement over weeks to a few months.

Impression: Right oculomotor (third) nerve palsy, pupil-involving, vascular imaging and MRI negative - presumed microvascular.

Plan / discharge 19:30:
- Patch or tape one lens to relieve double vision; alternate eyes.
- No driving while seeing double.
- Neuro-ophthalmology referral, to be seen in 2-3 weeks.
- Keep blood sugar and blood pressure well controlled; continue all home medications.
- Return immediately for severe headache, worsening droop or eye movement, new weakness, numbness or speech trouble.
- Follow up with PCP.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ER Monday - double vision
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I was in the ER Monday. Woke up and was seeing double, right eye wouldn't move right. They did a CT and an MRI, said no aneurysm or stroke, and that it's a nerve to the eye from the diabetes and pressure. Neurologist saw me there. Wearing a patch. Can't drive so my neighbor is helping. They want me to see an eye nerve specialist. Anything I should do?

documents.title: RE: ER Monday - double vision
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Darren - sorry you're dealing with this. We'll request the ER records so the doctor can review. Keep taking all your medicines, keep the patch on when you need it, and no driving until the double vision is gone. Go back to the ER right away for a bad headache, the eyelid or eye getting worse, or any weakness or trouble talking. Let us know if the neuro-ophthalmology office doesn't call you within a week. Your September 10 visit is still on.

documents.title: Records request - ED
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Requested 7/6/26 ED record including imaging and neurology consult from regional hospital. Received 7/14, scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: eye update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update. Double vision is a little better, I can go without the patch around the house now. Neuro eye doctor couldn't see me till September 3, I'm on their cancellation list. Still not driving. Sugars good.

documents.title: RE: eye update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it's starting to improve - that fits the ER's read. Keep the Sept 3 appointment and send us their note if they give you one. We'll go over everything on the 10th.
